name: Gertrudis Gómez de Avellaneda
image_credit: Federico de Madrazo y Kuntz · Public domain

checks.lead: Gertrudis Gómez de Avellaneda y Arteaga (March 23, 1814 – February 1, 1873)  was a 19th-century Cuban-born Spanish writer. Born in Puerto Príncipe, now Camagüey, she lived in Cuba until she was 22. Her family moved to Spain in 1836, where she started writing as La Peregrina (The Pilgrim) and lived there until 1859, when she moved back to Cuba with her second husband until his death in 1863, after which she moved back to Spain. She died in Madrid in 1873 from diabetes at the age of 58.
